audion.title: Audion: Turning a LinkedIn Click into a Lead
audion.subtitle: For Audion's US launch, I designed the landing page for its LinkedIn campaign, covering design, copywriting and Webflow implementation.
audion.team: Project Manager, SEO, Paid Search, Tracking
audion.contextP1a: Audion, an AI-powered audio advertising platform, was launching in the US with a LinkedIn ad campaign targeting CMOs. The offer: a 22-page white paper, the
audion.contextP1b: , exploring how US media budgets are allocated. My mission was to design the landing page visitors reached after clicking the ads and turn that traffic into qualified leads. I worked exclusively on this campaign page, not on Audion's main website.
audion.contextP2: I received the brief from the project manager and worked with the SEO, paid search and tracking teams. I also validated decisions with Audion's CMOs and sales team.
audion.challenge1Text: Most LinkedIn users browse on their phones, so the page had to be designed for mobile first.
audion.challenge2Text: After clicking an ad, visitors need to see the creative's promise reinforced within seconds.
audion.challenge3Text: Convince CMOs to share their contact details for a brand that was still relatively unknown in the US.
audion.challenge4Text: Prioritise lead generation while introducing Audion to visitors who land on the page.
audion.strategy1Text: Generate qualified leads through the form, then introduce Audion to visitors who land on the page.
audion.strategy2Text: A hero section focused on the white paper and form, followed by a content preview, social proof and an introduction to Audion.
audion.strategy3Text: A hero section combining the value proposition and form, followed by an 'Why audio?' section and a more detailed introduction to Audion.
audion.strategyConclusion: The final page follows Version A's structure, with an additional section on the benefits of audio drawn from Version B.
audion.decision1Text: The sales team wanted five fields to collect as much data as possible. I recommended limiting the form to two or three fields, as each additional field can reduce completion rates, especially on mobile. The final form has three fields: name, role (advertiser, agency or adtech) and work email.
audion.decision2Title: A hero section built to drive downloads
audion.decision2Text: Above the fold: a benefit-led headline, a visual of the report, a '22 pages' label, brand logos to build trust and the form.
audion.decision3Title: A thank-you page that extends the journey
audion.decision3Text: A download confirmation, followed by a call to action for Audion and three cards inviting visitors to explore further.
audion.decision4Text: There was no user testing on this project. I refined the page using my landing page experience and feedback from the sales team and CMOs. Iterations focused on the form, visuals, headline and copy, icons, logos and buttons.
audion.resultsText: The landing page was delivered and launched within six weeks, serving as the destination for LinkedIn ads. It sat at the bottom of the funnel, and traffic remained limited, so I don't have reliable conversion data to share.
audion.takeawaysText: Presenting two versions made the discussion more concrete. When discussing the form, framing the conversation around leads and completion rates helped me get buy-in from the sales team. My marketing background proved useful.
audion.nextStepsText: Test two headlines and two form lengths, then analyse mobile sessions to identify where visitors drop off.
